bundles.evidenceText: libertarian free will doesn't matter at all because having it wouldn't give you responsibility
bundles.rationale: The excerpt asserts that possessing libertarian free will would not confer responsibility. This supports the subsidiary indeterminacy bridge because an indeterministic or libertarian addition cannot rescue basic-desert control. The central bridge is the nearest competitor, but the excerpt does not assert its specific luck-to-sourcehood mechanism.

The excerpt asserts that causal determination must not be equated with absence of control and allows that causally shaped agents may retain strong self-control. This attacks the central sourcehood bridge's necessary inference from causation beyond the agent to deficient control or sourcehood. It does not attack the motion bridge, because no complete conclusion about basic desert or punishment is stated.

bundles.evidenceText: they matter in all kinds of important ways but they matter for different reasons
bundles.rationale: The excerpt asserts that compatibilist distinctions have value but are not sufficient grounds for desert-based moral practices. This attacks the motion bridge's claimed connection from adequate control to justified responsibility, blame, or punishment. The central-control bridge is excluded because the speaker does not deny that the distinctions identify real capacities and instead expressly grants that they matter.
